text.p: Norwegian oil company Statoil, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS, said on Monday it had awarded a 350 million NOK contract to Westminster Offshore AS, which is owned by Dutch firm Royal Boskalis.
Statoil said in a statement the deal with the Norwegian subsidiary of Royal Boskalis involved a five-year framework contract for offshore gravel dumping.
"Depending on the quantity of gravel involved, the contract is worth some NOK 350 million," it said.
Gravel-dumping services require precision placement of crushed stone from vessels to stabilise seabed pipelines and protect them from trawls and similar objects.
The contract will meet the need for gravel dumping on several pipelaying and development projects operated by Statoil.

These include the Aasgard field off mid-Norway, the Aasgard gas trunkline, the Gullfaks satellites development in the North Sea, and the Europipe II, NorFra and Ekofisk bypass gas lines, Statoil said.
